Subject: Fwd: Pleiades3b intermittent errors — initial triage

Internal notes / initial triage: forwarding what I pulled from infra.

--- Forwarded internal trace summary ---
Time window: 2025-07-09T08:28:00Z - 2025-07-09T08:55:00Z
Symptoms: ~8% of requests to route pleiades3b returned 504 or 500 (model-hang). Error spike correlated with high goroutine wait time on a subset of GPU workers.
Observed behaviors:
- Elevated kernel queue latency on a sub-pool of Trident-A GPUs (region-us-east-1a).
- KV cache eviction rate increased (short-lived TTL pressure) for large context workloads.
- One worker (gpu-node-pla-12) exhibited a 30–90s stall before returning a 500 model-hang; restart/reset of that worker cleared the malaise.

Initial hypothesis: a resource scheduling bug combined with a recent micro-optimizer change for attention tiling that was rolled 2025-07-08 23:10 UTC; the optimizer exposes a race in the kernel queue under specific batch/ctx distributions leading to worker stalls.

Immediate mitigations applied (09:10–09:22 UTC):
- Isolated and drained gpu-node-pla-12.
- Rolled back micro-optimizer change in the serving pool for pleiades3b (safemode -> previous optimizer).
- Bounced the remaining nodes in the affected sub-pool to force fresh kernel scheduling.

Status: error rate reduced to baseline (~0.3%) by 09:18 UTC. Continuing to monitor.

Planned follow-ups:
- Produce a diagnostic bundle (attached) with request traces, kernel logs, and node snapshots.
- Patch the scheduling logic to avoid the observed race (JIRA-OPS-3219).
- Recommend customers keep a short retry/backoff window for transient 5xx during the rollout window (we'll update recommended client settings).

Ben
SRE Lead | Redwood Inference

Attachment: pleiades3b_diag_20250709.tar.gz (tgz, 12MB)

From: marcus_lin@redwood.example.com
To: rachel_kim@redwood.example.com, ben_carter@redwood.example.com
Date: 2025-07-09T10:02:45Z
Subject: Re: Pleiades3b elevated server errors — recovery note & remediation checklist

Adding runtime analysis and proposed customer-facing mitigations.

RCA (concise):
- Root cause: a race condition in kernel queue scheduling introduced by the attention-tiling micro-optimizer (rolled 2025-07-08). Under particular batch mixes (small batches + occasional long-context requests) the queue depth accounting could underflow, causing a worker to appear idle while GPU kernels were stuck in flight, resulting in long stalls and occasional 500 model-hang.
- Why only some customers: the spike correlated with Starlite's mix of short interactive sessions with periodic long-history context syncs — the mix triggers the queue contention scenario more often.

Customer mitigation checklist (we should send these as clear steps):
1) Client-side: set a retry policy that treats 5xx and 504 as transient; retry up to 3 times with exponential backoff starting at 150ms.
2) Timeout tuning: if you currently set >60s client timeout, consider lowering to 30s while we finish patch. Shorter timeouts reduce risk of blocking client threads on stalled workers.
3) Fallback: add a non-blocking fallback to pleiades3b:v1 or a smaller latency-optimized variant for ephemeral assistant responses.
4) Streaming: if you're using streaming, consider checkpointing partial outputs to avoid data loss on retry.
5) Monitoring: enable token-level sampling for 10m windows so we can correlate individual traces (we can enable server-side sampling for you if desired).

Operational commitments:
- Patch for scheduler race targeted for 2025-07-11 02:00 UTC (JIRA-OPS-3219).
- Post-patch canary and progressive rollout across regions with extended sampling.
- We will provide a follow-up with before/after error-rate histograms and a short write-up on why the optimizer triggered the race.

I'll draft the customer-facing recovery note and remediation checklist; Rachel, if you want to send a single consolidated message with attaches and the checklist, I'll sign off.

Thanks — Marcus
Senior Runtime Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Pleiades3b incident — recovery summary, RCA, and recommended customer actions

Hi Emily — apologies again for the disruption last week. Below is a concise summary, the root cause, and a short action checklist your engineering team can implement immediately. Please let me know if you'd like us to apply any of these changes on your behalf.

Summary of what happened
- Window: 2025-07-09 08:28–08:55 UTC.
- Impact: intermittent 5xx (model-hang / 500) and 504 responses affecting ~8% of requests in the window for Starlite's Pleiades3b route. Error rate returned to baseline after mitigations.

Root cause (high level)- A scheduling race introduced by a recent micro-optimizer for attention tiling caused worker stalls under certain batch/context mixes. This produced elevated kernel queue latency and occasional model-hang errors on a subset of GPU workers.

What we did- Drained and restarted the affected worker node.
- Rolled back the micro-optimizer change in the Pleiades3b serving pool.
- Bounced remaining nodes in the affected sub-pool to flush kernel queues.
- Produced a diagnostic bundle (attached) and opened JIRA-OPS-3219 to track the scheduling patch and rollout plan.

Customer action checklist (recommended immediate steps)
1) Implement a transient-retry policy for 5xx/504 (max 3 attempts, exponential backoff starting at 150ms).
2) If possible, lower your client timeout to 30s while we complete the rollout.
3) Add a fallback model variant (pleiades3b:v1 or a latency-optimized small model) for short responses.
4) If you use streaming, checkpoint partial responses so user state is preserved on retry.
5) Share a short sampling window (10 minutes) of failing request-ids if you can — we can then provide correlated server logs.

Attachments: pleiades3b_diag_20250709.tar.gz (diagnostic bundle), request-trace-pleiades-08-50-23.json

Compensation and next steps
- We're proposing a small credit (one week of embedded API usage equivalent) for the affected window; I'll follow up with finance to formalize.
- We'll send a post-patch brief with before/after error-rate charts and an engineering summary of the scheduling fix once JIRA-OPS-3219 is complete.

If you'd like, we can schedule a 30-minute call early next week to walk your engineers through the mitigation checklist and apply any config changes.

Thanks for your patience — please ping me if you see any recurrences.

Best,
